top_entities.name: Nepal
top_entities.news_summary: Nepal-Tibet border flash-flood/glacier-collapse disaster (originating 2026-08-26 on Langtang Lirung) death toll reached 1,114 in Nepal per an NDRRMA update reported 2026-09-02 (plus 16 dead / ~546 missing on the Chinese side); ~3,916 missing in Nepal. CNN/ABC/Al Jazeera coverage (2026-09-01/09-02) found no glacier-hazard early-warning system existed for the affected area, Nepal's SMS alert system failed or arrived late and Nepali-only, and satellite imagery showed visible glacier instability days before collapse -- a repeat of an unaddressed 2022 recommendation after a similar 2021 disaster. A later-aggregated figure of 1,259 dead / 5,083 missing appeared only in an undated Wikipedia-sourced aggregation and is deliberately NOT used here per the death-toll verification discipline -- the dated NDRRMA figure of 1,114 is used instead.

top_entities.name: Jamaica
top_entities.news_summary: Jamaica's government signed contracts on 2026-09-03 worth roughly JMD $1 billion (approx. US$6.3M at ~158 JMD/USD -- NOT US$1B; the source article specifies the JMD denomination) for delivery of 268 semi-permanent housing solutions (143 in Westmoreland, 125 in St Elizabeth) for families displaced by Hurricane Melissa (Oct 2025 landfall; ~120,000 buildings lost roofs; ~US$8.8B physical damage per World Bank/IDB). Units financed via the National Housing Trust plus a housing donation from the Government of China. At ~US$23,500 per unit for semi-permanent (not full-permanent) housing, the figure is plausible and proportionate -- a moderate, dated, positive humanitarian/governance response. Single-sourced (Jamaica Observer only); no second independent outlet located this cycle to corroborate the exact contract value, which the assessor should treat as a limitation, not a disqualifier, given the day-precision dated primary source.

top_entities.name: Boeing
top_entities.news_summary: The FAA confirmed to wire services on 2026-09-02 that Boeing paid a $3,139,319 civil penalty (proposed September 2025) for quality-system violations connected to the January 2024 Alaska Airlines door-plug blowout (hundreds of violations at the 737 Renton plant and the Spirit AeroSystems Wichita fuselage facility, including an employee pressuring an FAA-delegated co-worker to sign off a non-airworthy 737 MAX). Boeing paid this quietly in January 2026 without public disclosure; the payment only became public on 2026-09-02 via Reuters/AP wire coverage -- a 5+ month disclosure delay relevant to transparency/governance scoring. last_assessed (2026-06-10) predates this disclosure.

NOTE: a later-aggregated figure of 1,259 dead / 5,083 missing appeared in search results (Wikipedia-sourced) but could not be tied to a dated primary source inside the window and is NOT used as the evidence figure here -- flagged per the superlative/death-toll verification discipline.
